To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
histones can be divided into three groups according the binding strength to DNA.
the histone H1 is the weakest and histone H3 + H2A the strongest histones binding to DNA.

The dissociation of H1, H3 + H2A and H3 + H3 + H5 from DNA was shown by treating the whole DNA--histone complex with high concentration of whole histone in the medium of ionic strength (NaCl) 0.15M and 0.7mM Na-phosphate buffer (pH 7.0).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dissociation of the histone--DNA complexes in the physiological medium and the changes of histone content in the nucleosome.

the binding of histones to DNA in the medium of low ionic strength (1.0 mM Na-phosphate, pH 7,0) and high ionic strength (150 mM NaCl + 1.0 mM sodium phosphate, pH 7) and with the dissociation of histone fractions from DNA.
the binding strength of the histone fraction with DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding strength of the histone fractions with nucleosomal DNA is different.
there is no single histone--DNA interaction, but a variety of interactions, which are dependent on the histone type and the histone--DNA stoichiometry.
the histones H2B and/or H2A are not bound as tightly to the nucleosomal DNA as the other histones.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a hierarchy of histone--DNA interaction and that the binding of histones to DNA is not a static but a dynamic process.
the histone octamer does not have a constant composition and the nucleosome is not an invariant structure.
the nucleosome is a reversible formation, and that the binding strength of the histones to DNA is not the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that
histone variants are not randomly distributed in the genome.
we can use histone binding strength to DNA to predict how histones will behave under various conditions.
the histone content can vary between cells and tissues and can change in response to physiological stimuli.
